beats.caption: Say Maya kept her $100 piece of Sunny Juice. Its worth swings up and down. A great summer lifts it to $200.
beats.a11y: Maya beside Sunny Juice at night. A customer walks up to the counter. Below, lesson 1's ten pieces, hers purple, grow to twice as tall.

beats.caption: A rainy year drops it to $150. It fell $50 from its $200 high: 25% of that high. That's its drawdown.
beats.a11y: Rain at the stall and no customers. The ten pieces shrink to three quarters of their height, a dotted line left where their tops were.

beats.caption: Money in an insured bank doesn't drop like that, but it grows slowly. What can grow more can also drop more.
beats.a11y: Maya at the stone bank. A shield shines over the vault door, and a small coin slowly appears beside it.

beats.caption: Atlas asks: why own a piece at all, if it can drop like that?
beats.a11y: Maya walks out into the orchard under the moon. Atlas, floating in the sky, does a little hop.

mix.title: Bonds, stocks, or a mix
mix.footer: Since 1928. Green: average growth a year. Amber: worst year's drop. Source: NYU Stern.

states.caption: Bonds can drop in worth too, before they're paid back. US government bonds grew least and dropped least.
states.a11y: On the slate, under a teal tab: a short green bar up and an amber bar down. Maya looks on.

states.caption: A mix: half bonds, half stocks, kept that way each year. Both its bars land in between.
states.a11y: Under a half teal, half purple tab, a taller green bar up and a longer amber bar down.

states.caption: Big US stocks: the most growth of the three, and by far the deepest worst year, 1931.
states.a11y: Under a purple tab, the tallest green bar up and an amber bar down twice as long as the mix had.

longer.title: Big US stocks, kept longer
longer.footer: Big US stocks, counting cash paid to owners, 1928 to 2025. Source: NYU Stern.

states.caption: Each square is one year since 1928. Big US stocks as a group lost money in the 26 amber ones.
states.a11y: On the slate, 98 small squares, one for each year since 1928, in rows by decade: mostly green, with 26 amber, many in the 1930s.

states.caption: Now each square is 10 years in a row, starting that year. Just 5 of the 89 stretches lost money.
states.a11y: The squares change: one for each 10-year stretch. Only 5 are amber, the stretches that started in 1928, 1929, 1930, 1999 and 2000.

states.caption: Kept 20 years at a time, none of the 79 stretches lost money. Same stocks, just a longer wait.
states.a11y: One square for each 20-year stretch since 1928, and every one is green.
